mainTopic: Selling holy community property and a בית הכנסת, the רבית question on רבי מאיר, urinating near a place of prayer, and stories of Sages' long lives
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ruling that charity goes to the local חבר עיר, and רב הונא adds that the poor of both towns rely on him. A new משנה follows. רבי מאיר forbids selling a community's holy item to an individual, while the רבנן say that by his logic even a sale from a big town to a small town would be forbidden. A second משנה gives three views on selling a בית הכנסת: רבי מאיר allows it only with a buy-back condition, the חכמים allow a permanent sale except for four disgraceful uses, and רבי יהודה allows a sale 'as a courtyard' with no limits. The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר's buy-back sale avoids רבית. It answers with צד אחד ברבית, and רבא offers a different reading of that dispute. Next comes שמואל's ruling that one may urinate within four אמות of where he prayed, and a ברייתא that is corrected so that one must only wait, not move away, after praying or urinating. רב אשי explains that the prayer is still on a person's lips. The amud ends with stories of Sages explaining their long lives, including רבי זכאי and רב הונא's sacrifices for קידוש wine. רבי פרידא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If a town scholar exists, the charity goes to him
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the earlier ruling: when there is a חבר עיר, the charity money is handed over to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [This applies only where there is no] town scholar, but if there is a town scholar there, it should be given to the town scholar.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of an earlier answer. The rule is that charity money goes to the local חבר עיר, the man in charge of communal needs, whenever there is one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full rule had a limit. Visitors take their charity home with them only when there is no חבר עיר. When there is one, he decides how the money is used. This is the basis for leaving the money with רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Town scholar / communal supervisor who manages the community's needs, including charity

phrases.english: a town scholar,
phrases.notes: This finishes the line that started on the previous amud: 'this applies only when there is no town scholar.'

phrases.english: but if there is a town scholar there —
it should be given to the town scholar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל יֵשׁ שָׁם חֲבֵר עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion from the previous amud
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When a חבר עיר is present, charity collected in his town is given to him to manage.

steps.title: All the more so, since both towns' poor rely on me
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא strengthens the ruling: the money certainly belongs with him, because the poor of both his town and the visitors' town depend on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so here, since my poor and your poor both rely on me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a כל שכן, an 'even more so' argument, to show the money should stay with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule already gives the money to a חבר עיר. Here there is an extra reason: רב הונא supports the poor of the visitors' own town too. So he is the right person to distribute it, and the earlier discussion closes.
steps.whatToRemember: Charity goes to the local חבר עיר when there is one. רב הונא fits this rule even more strongly, because both towns' poor depend on him.

phrases.english: And all the more so
since my poor and your poor
rely upon me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן דְּעַנְיֵי דִּידִי וְדִידְכוּ עֲלַי סְמִיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger reason (כל שכן) to apply the rule of step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The charity stays with רב הונא, the חבר עיר who supports the poor of both towns.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a community's holy item may not be sold to an individual
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי מאיר forbids selling a community-owned holy item to a private person, because that lowers its level of קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not sell something belonging to the public to an individual, because that lowers it from its holiness. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. רבי מאיר states that a community's holy item, such as a בית הכנסת, may not be sold to a single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the buyer keeps using the item for the same holy purpose, רבי מאיר thinks something is lost. Holiness that belongs to many people is a higher level than holiness belonging to one person. Selling to an individual therefore 'brings it down' from its קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: They lower it from its holiness

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not say the item loses its holiness entirely. He means its level of holiness drops, because fewer people use it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹכְרִין אֶת שֶׁל רַבִּים לְיָחִיד,
phrases.english: They may not sell that which belongs to the community to an individual,
phrases.notes: Referring to a sacred object such as a synagogue

phrases.english: because they lower it from its sanctity,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹכְרִין אֶת שֶׁל רַבִּים לְיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the charity discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a community's holy item may not be sold to an individual, because it would drop to a lower level of קדושה.

steps.title: The Rabbis: then a big town couldn't sell to a small town either
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רבי מאיר: if fewer users means lower holiness, then selling from a large town to a small town should also be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, then it should also not be allowed from a large town to a small town.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, the רבנן attack רבי מאיר's reasoning by pointing to a case everyone allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small town also has fewer people than a large town. If fewer users really lowered the holiness, that sale would be forbidden too. Since such a sale is clearly allowed, the רבנן conclude that selling to an individual should be allowed as well.

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לֹא מֵעִיר גְּדוֹלָה לְעִיר קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: then also not from a large town to a small town.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן אַף לֹא מֵעִיר גְּדוֹלָה לְעִיר קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's reasoning in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reason that fewer users lowers holiness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same reasoning would forbid a sale from a large town to a small town, which is obviously allowed.

steps.title: The גמרא: the Rabbis' argument sounds strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by noting that the רבנן made a good point. How would רבי מאיר answer it?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן are speaking well to רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by saying the רבנן's argument seems convincing. This sets up the next step, where it explains how רבי מאיר would respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grammatically this is just praise, but its job is a challenge: it puts pressure on רבי מאיר. The גמרא now owes us his defense.

keyTerms.meaning: They are saying well / they make a good point

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Well are they saying to him —
the Rabbis to Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the רבנן's challenge from step 4 and asks for רבי מאיר's defense
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's position in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The large-town to small-town comparison seems to defeat רבי מאיר's reason.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a small town is still a community, an individual is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר distinguishes the cases. Moving the item to a smaller town keeps its community-level holiness. Moving it to an individual removes that level.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? From a large town to a small town: before, it was holy, and now too it is holy. From a community to an individual, there is no such holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי מאיר by showing the two cases are different in kind, not just in size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, what matters is whether the item belongs to a community. A small town is still a community, so the item keeps its community-level קדושה. An individual is not a community, so that level of holiness is lost.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי מאיר is not counting heads. He draws a line between communal and private ownership.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir [would answer]:
from a large town to a small town —
originally it was sacred,
and now too it is sacred.
From a community to an individual, there is no [such] sanctity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, מֵעִיר גְּדוֹלָה לְעִיר קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 4 and 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any drop in the number of users lowers the holiness, so the small-town sale should also be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Communal holiness stays the same whatever the community's size. Only a transfer to an individual removes it.

steps.title: The Rabbis: fewer people is a concern either way, because of 'the king's glory'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי מאיר's distinction. If fewer users mattered, it would matter for a smaller town too, based on בְּרוֹב עָם הַדְרַת מֶלֶךְ. Since it does not stop that sale, it should not stop a sale to an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If there is a concern, then in a case like this too there is a concern, because of 'In the multitude of people is the king's glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the רבנן's answer to רבי מאיר's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the 'community versus individual' line is not real. The only possible concern is honor to ה׳, and that honor grows with the number of people, as the פסוק says. A smaller town also has fewer people. Since we allow that sale anyway, a sale to an individual should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is reason to be concerned
'In the multitude of people is the king's glory' (משלי 14:28)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: community holiness is a category, so a small town keeps it and an individual loses it. רבנן: the only issue is the number of people (רוב עם), and that issue applies to a small town too. Since a small-town sale is allowed, a sale to an individual is allowed as well.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis [would respond]:
if there is cause for concern,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא נָמֵי אִיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ,
phrases.english: then in a case like this too there is cause for concern,
because of 'In the multitude of people is the king's glory.'
phrases.notes: That's a פסוק in משלי 14:28.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אִי אִיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא נָמֵי אִיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's distinction from step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's claim that a smaller community keeps the same level of holiness
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Honor to ה׳ depends on the number of people (רוב עם), so a smaller town is also a drop. Since that drop does not forbid a sale, neither should the drop to an individual.

steps.title: Three opinions on selling a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר allows selling a בית הכנסת only with a buy-back condition. The חכמים allow a permanent sale, except for four disgraceful uses. רבי יהודה allows a sale 'as a courtyard,' and then the buyer may do whatever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בית הכנסת may only be sold on condition that the sellers can take it back whenever they want. This is the view of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say it may be sold forever, except for four uses: a bathhouse, a tannery, a מקוה, or a bathroom. רבי יהודה says it may be sold 'to be a courtyard,' and then the buyer may do with it whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives three opinions about how a town may sell its בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not state רבי מאיר's reason; he only allows a sale on the condition that the town can take it back. The חכמים allow a permanent sale and simply ban four disgraceful uses. רבי יהודה goes furthest: once it is sold as a plain courtyard, the buyer is not restricted at all.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition (here, that the sellers may take it back)
A tannery, a place where hides are processed and which smells bad
Sold for the purpose of being a courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two רבי יהודה rulings. Here in the משנה he talks about selling a בית הכנסת. In the next steps the גמרא brings a different ruling of his, about רבית.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
They may not sell a synagogue
except on a condition,
that if they want, they can take it back,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ מִמְכַּר עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: they may sell it as a permanent sale,
except for four things:
for a bathhouse, or for a tannery,
for ritual immersion, or for a lavatory.
phrases.notes: These uses would be disrespectful to the building's former holiness.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָהּ לְשֵׁם חָצֵר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: they may sell it for the purpose of a courtyard,
and the buyer may do whatever he wants with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מוֹכְרִין בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת אֶלָּא עַל תְּנַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion about lowering levels of קדושה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: sell only with a buy-back condition. חכמים: a permanent sale is allowed, except for four disgraceful uses. רבי יהודה: sell as a courtyard, and then the buyer may use it freely.

steps.title: How can buyers live there without it being interest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר. If the sale can be undone, the purchase money is really like a loan, so living in the building looks like רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: According to רבי מאיר, how can the buyers live in it? That is רבית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי מאיר's conditional sale by arguing that it creates a problem of רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sellers later take the building back, they return the money. Looking back, the money was a loan from the buyers to the sellers. Meanwhile the buyers got free use of the building, which is a benefit for lending money. That is forbidden as רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: How may they live in it?
Interest, meaning any benefit a lender gets for a loan (forbidden)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But according to Rabbi Meir,
how may they (the buyers) live in it?
Isn't this interest!
phrases.notes: If the sale is undone, the money was really a loan, and the buyers' living there was payment for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הֵיכִי דָּיְירִי בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a בית הכנסת may be sold only on condition that the sellers can take it back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sale that can be reversed turns the payment into a possible loan. The buyer's use of the property then counts as forbidden benefit, which is רבית.

steps.title: רבי מאיר holds that uncertain interest is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that רבי מאיר follows רבי יהודה, who holds that צד אחד ברבית, a case that might or might not turn into interest, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי מאיר said this following the view of רבי יהודה, who says that 'one side of interest' (uncertain interest) is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by linking רבי מאיר to a known view of רבי יהודה about uncertain רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sellers may never ask for the building back. In that case it was a real sale and there was never a loan. Since it is only possibly רבית, רבי יהודה allows it, and רבי מאיר agrees with that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncertain interest, a deal that only might turn out to be interest

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a key category in the laws of רבית: a deal that only possibly becomes a loan is treated differently from a definite loan.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said it following the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: uncertain (one-sided) interest is permitted.
phrases.notes: It is uncertain because the sale may never be undone, so there may never be a loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבית challenge against רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to an existing view (שיטה) that permits uncertain רבית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed that any reversible sale where the buyer benefits is forbidden רבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, possible רבית (צד אחד) is permitted, and רבי מאיר follows that view.

steps.title: A ברייתא about selling a field to a creditor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא where רבי יהודה's view appears. A debtor sells his field to his creditor in place of the debt. The first opinion permits this only if the seller eats the produce, not the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Someone was owed a מנה (100 זוז) by his friend, and the friend made his field into a sale for him. When the seller eats the produce, it is permitted. When the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the source for רבי יהודה's view. This first part is the setup: the ruling of the first opinion in the ברייתא. רבי יהודה's own opinion follows next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debtor sells his field to the lender with the right to buy it back if he gets money. If the buyer (the lender) eats the produce and the field is later bought back, he has benefited from a loan, so the first opinion forbids it. This sets up the contrast with רבי יהודה, who is about to permit it because the רבית is only uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: Was owed money by his fellow (a creditor)
Eats (enjoys) the produce of the field

steps.confusionAlert: The 'מותר / אסור' at the end of this text is NOT רבי יהודה's view. It is the first opinion in the ברייתא. רבי יהודה's lenient view comes right after this.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
If one was owed a maneh (100 dinars) by his fellow,
and he (the debtor) made his field a sale to him,
phrases.notes: A conditional sale: the debtor may buy it back if he gets money.

phrases.english: when the seller eats the produce, it is permitted,
if the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The buyer would be benefiting from what may turn out to be a loan.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה נוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that is the source for רבי יהודה's view cited by רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds צד אחד ברבית מותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a debtor who sells his field to his creditor. This first part gives the first opinion's ruling, which sets up רבי יהודה's dissent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה permits even the buyer to eat the produce
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה says that even if the buyer eats the produce of the field, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even if the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from the last step. Now it gives רבי יהודה's opinion, which disagrees with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A debtor sold his field to his creditor in place of the debt, and he may pay back the debt and take back the field. The first opinion forbids the buyer to eat the produce, because if the field goes back, the produce would have been payment for waiting on a loan. רבי יהודה permits it, because the field might never go back. This is the source showing that רבי יהודה permits צד אחד ברבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The buyer (here, the creditor who receives the field)
Eats the produce, meaning he enjoys the field's crops

steps.whyThisMatters: This line proves רבי יוחנן's claim from step 10: רבי יהודה permits a case that may or may not turn into רבית, so רבי מאיר's buy-back sale of a בית הכנסת can follow him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: Since the sale may never be undone, it is only possible interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ לוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 11 by giving the disputing opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the creditor-buyer may eat the produce of a field sold to him in place of a debt.

steps.title: רבי יהודה brings a story about ביתוס בן זונין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: ביתוס בן זונין sold his field this way, guided by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer ate the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with ביתוס בן זונין, who made a sale of his field under the guidance of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer was eating the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a real-life story as proof that a great sage allowed the buyer to eat the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה claims that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה approved this very arrangement. If so, a major authority permitted the buyer to eat the produce even though the sale might be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident, used as proof

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Baitos ben Zunen
who made his field a sale
phrases.notes: A conditional sale in place of a debt.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: under the guidance of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
and the buyer was eating the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבַיְתוֹס בֶּן זוֹנִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a precedent to support רבי יהודה's ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that the buyer may eat the produce
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of ביתוס בן זונין, whose sale was approved by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה

steps.title: The Sages say the seller ate the produce in that story
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. In the story of ביתוס, it was the seller who ate the produce, not the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? The seller was eating the produce, not the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The other sages push back on רבי יהודה's story. They say he has the facts wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not argue about the rule here. They argue about what happened. If the seller ate the produce, the story fits the first opinion and proves nothing for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? Used to reject a proof

phrases.english: They said to him:
Is there a proof from there?!
The seller was eating the produce
and not the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the story brought as proof in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story; the rule itself is not directly attacked here.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The facts were reported wrongly; in the real case the seller, not the buyer, ate the produce.

steps.title: What is the real point of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle separates רבי יהודה and the first opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what the argument is really about. This short question sets up the answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the result: one side lets the buyer eat the produce and the other does not. Now the גמרא wants the underlying principle that causes the disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? Asks for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story and its rejection, the גמרא steps back to analyze the dispute itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle behind the dispute between the first opinion and רבי יהודה

steps.title: They argue about possible interest
steps.stepSummary: They argue about צד אחד ברבית. רבי יהודה permits it, and the first opinion forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Possible interest is the difference between them. One sage holds that possible interest is permitted, and the other holds that possible interest is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about a deal that might or might not turn into interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the debtor never pays and the field stays sold, the buyer simply ate his own crops. If the debtor pays and takes the field back, the produce was payment for a loan. רבי יהודה permits this uncertain case, and the first opinion forbids it. This matches רבי יוחנן's reading from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Possible interest: a deal that might or might not become interest

steps.confusionAlert: צד אחד ברבית does not mean a small amount of interest. It means a deal where we do not yet know whether it will turn out to be interest at all.

phrases.english: Possible interest
is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: One sage holds: possible interest is permitted,
phrases.notes: That's רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and the other sage holds: possible interest is forbidden.
phrases.notes: That's the first opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether צד אחד ברבית is permitted (רבי יהודה) or forbidden (the first opinion).

steps.title: רבא: they argue about interest that will be returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone forbids possible interest. The argument is about רבית על מנת להחזיר, interest given on condition that it be paid back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that possible interest is forbidden. Here, the difference between them is interest given on condition that it be returned. One sage holds that interest on condition that it be returned is permitted, and the other holds it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the same argument. In his view, both sides forbid possible interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explains that the buyer ate the produce on condition that, if the field goes back, he will repay the value of the produce. רבי יהודה permits this, because if it ever turns into a loan, the lender gives back his gain. The first opinion forbids it anyway. According to רבא, this ברייתא no longer shows that רבי יהודה permits צד אחד ברבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest given on condition that it will be returned

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the dispute. The first reading says it is about צד אחד ברבית, which fits רבי יוחנן. רבא says it is about רבית על מנת להחזיר.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר,
phrases.english: According to everyone, possible interest is forbidden,
and here, interest on condition that it be returned
is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: רִבִּית עַל מְנָת לְהַחֲזִיר מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: One sage holds: interest on condition that it be returned is permitted,
phrases.notes: That's רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: and the other sage holds: it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: That's the first opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing answer to the question of step 15, replacing the explanation of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone forbids צד אחד ברבית. The dispute is whether רבית על מנת להחזיר is permitted (רבי יהודה) or forbidden (the first opinion).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's reading removes the support for רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי מאיר, since according to רבא, רבי יהודה does not permit צד אחד ברבית.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the Sages allow a permanent sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where the חכמים say a בית הכנסת may be sold with a permanent sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: They may sell it with a permanent sale, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of interest and quotes the next part of the משנה. This line sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allowed a permanent sale except for four disgraceful uses (step 8). By quoting this line, the גמרא signals a new discussion connected to respecting a holy place.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote continues as in the source

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
They may sell it with a permanent sale, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ מִמְכַּר עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the interest discussion and returns to the משנה's next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים permit a permanent sale of a בית הכנסת, except for disgraceful uses.

steps.title: שמואל: one may urinate within four cubits of prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says in the name of שמואל that a person may urinate within four אמות of where he prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: It is permitted for a person to urinate within four cubits of prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from שמואל about the space around a place of prayer. It opens a new topic connected to the משנה's concern for respecting holy places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits disgraceful uses of a former בית הכנסת. שמואל teaches that the spot where a person prayed does not gain that kind of holiness. Even within four אמות of it, urinating is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a בית הכנסת building. It is about the spot where a person just prayed, which does not become a holy place.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is permitted for a person to urinate
within four cubits of prayer.
phrases.notes: Even right where he prayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מוּתָּר לָאָדָם לְהַשְׁתִּין מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting the חכמים's view, the גמרא brings a related rule about respect for a place of prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may urinate within four אמות of the place where he prayed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: שמואל's ruling is already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what שמואל adds, since the משנה already lets a sold בית הכנסת be used for anything, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is שמואל teaching us? We already learned it in the משנה. רבי יהודה says: they may sell a synagogue for use as a plain courtyard, and the buyer may do whatever he wants with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges שמואל's ruling from step 19. He says it teaches nothing new, because the משנה already implies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets a sold בית הכנסת become anything, even a bathroom. If a whole בית הכנסת loses its holiness that easily, then four אמות where someone happened to pray certainly have no lasting holiness. So urinating there is obviously allowed, and שמואל's statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (i.e., this is already known)
For the purpose of a plain courtyard (any ordinary use)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: The גמרא often asks this when a statement seems to add nothing new.

phrases.english: We already learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They may sell it (a synagogue) for use as a courtyard,
and the buyer may do with it whatever he wishes.
phrases.notes: This includes even a disrespectful use, such as a bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 19 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one may urinate within four אמות of where he prayed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from רבי יהודה in the משנה: if a whole בית הכנסת can be used for anything, four אמות of prayer surely can too. So the ruling is unnecessary.

steps.title: Even the Sages would agree about the four cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that even the רבנן are strict only for a בית הכנסת, whose holiness is permanent. Four אמות of prayer have no permanent holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the Rabbis say their stricter ruling only about a synagogue, whose holiness is permanent. But the four cubits where someone prayed have no permanent holiness, so even the Rabbis would not forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף strengthens his challenge. He shows that the משנה makes שמואל's ruling obvious even according to the stricter opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say: the רבנן argue with רבי יהודה, so maybe שמואל is teaching us their view. רב יוסף answers that the רבנן are strict only because a בית הכנסת is set aside as holy for good. A spot where someone happened to pray was never set aside, so everyone agrees it has no lasting holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the חכמים of the משנה, who are stricter than רבי יהודה and forbid four disgraceful uses)
Four cubits (about 2 meters), the space around where a person prayed

steps.whyThisMatters: This draws a key line in the sugya: lasting holiness belongs to a place set aside as holy, like a בית הכנסת, not to any spot where someone once prayed.

phrases.english: And even the Rabbis do not say (their stricter ruling)
except about a synagogue, whose holiness is permanent.
But four cubits (where one prayed),
whose holiness is not permanent: no (even the Rabbis would not forbid it).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא קָאָמְרִי אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב יוסף's challenge so it holds even according to the רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל's ruling is obvious according to all opinions in the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reason behind the רבנן's strictness: a בית הכנסת has permanent holiness, and four אמות do not.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: שמואל's ruling seems obvious. A sold בית הכנסת can be used for anything (רבי יהודה), and even the רבנן are strict only because a בית הכנסת has permanent holiness. A spot where someone prayed has none.

steps.title: A ברייתא requires four cubits between prayer and urinating
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב נחמן. It says to move four אמות after praying before urinating, and to move four אמות after urinating before praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: One who prayed should move four cubits away and then urinate. And one who urinated should move four cubits away and then pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two rules about distance between prayer and urinating. This sets up רב נחמן's reaction in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule seems to say that the place of prayer keeps some holiness, which clashes with שמואל and רב יוסף. The second rule is about keeping prayer away from something unclean. רב נחמן will treat the two rules very differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (a reciter of ברייתות) taught before him

steps.confusionAlert: Here תַּנָּא does not mean a sage of the משנה period. It means a professional reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Nachman:
One who prayed should move four cubits away and then urinate,
and one who urinated should move four cubits away and then pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source on the same topic as שמואל's ruling. Its first clause seems to disagree with him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Move four אמות after praying before urinating, and move four אמות after urinating before praying.

steps.title: רב נחמן accepts the second rule from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that one who urinated must move four אמות before praying. A משנה in ברכות already teaches a four-אמות distance from urine and excrement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I can understand the rule that one who urinated should move four cubits away and then pray. We learned in a משנה: How far must one keep from urine and excrement? Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts his response by accepting the second half of the ברייתא. The word בשלמא ("granted") signals that a challenge to the first half is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second rule makes sense because prayer must be kept away from something unclean, like urine. A משנה in ברכות (22b) already sets that distance at four אמות. So this half has a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / I can understand (sets up a contrast with a harder case)
How far must one keep away?

phrases.english: He (Rav Nachman) said to him: Granted,
one who urinated moves four cubits away and then prays:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵינָא: כַּמָּה יַרְחִיק מֵהֶן וּמִן הַצּוֹאָה,
phrases.english: we learned: How far must one keep from them (urine) and from excrement?
phrases.notes: Quoted from משנה ברכות 22b.

phrases.english: Four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the second clause of the ברייתא as a setup for challenging the first clause.
steps.raayaObject: The second clause of the ברייתא: one who urinated moves four אמות before praying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה ברכות 22b: one must keep four אמות from urine and excrement.

steps.title: רב נחמן rejects the first rule: all of נהרדעא would be holy
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks why one would need to move four אמות after praying. If that were the law, every street in נהרדעא would be holy, and urinating would be forbidden everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need the rule that one who prayed should move four cubits away and then urinate? If so, you have made every street in Nehardea holy!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the first half of the ברייתא. He shows that it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a spot where someone prayed stays holy, urinating there would always be forbidden. People pray everywhere, so every street in נהרדעא would be off limits. That cannot be right, and it matches רב יוסף's point that prayer does not give a place permanent holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? / What is the reason for this?
נהרדעא, a major Jewish city in Babylonia

phrases.english: But: one who prayed moves four cubits away
and then urinates: why do I need this?
If so, you have sanctified
all the streets of Nehardea.
phrases.notes: People have surely prayed on every street, so urinating would be forbidden everywhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל מַרְחִיק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּמַשְׁתִּין לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting the second clause, רב נחמן challenges the first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first clause of the ברייתא: one who prayed must move four אמות before urinating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: if prayer made a spot holy, every street where people prayed would be forbidden for urinating.

steps.title: Fix the ברייתא: wait instead of moving away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's wording is corrected. After praying, one should wait (the time it takes to walk four אמות) before urinating, rather than move four אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach the ברייתא this way: he should wait (the time it takes to walk four cubits).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording to answer רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about the place, so the spot does not become holy. It is about time: one waits the time it takes to walk four אמות. This removes the problem of all of נהרדעא becoming holy, and it fits שמואל's ruling that one may urinate within four אמות. The reason for waiting after praying is not yet clear; the גמרא asks about it in the next step, and רב אשי answers in step 27.
steps.whatToRemember: The spot where a person prayed has no lasting holiness, so one may urinate there (שמואל). The corrected ברייתא is about time, not place. After praying, one waits about the time it takes to walk four אמות before urinating. After urinating, one waits the same amount of time before praying.
steps.confusionAlert: After the correction, both halves of the ברייתא are about waiting, not moving away. One who prayed waits the time it takes to walk four אמות before urinating. One who urinated waits the same amount of time before praying. Step 26 gives the reason for the second wait (droplets), and step 27 gives the reason for the first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This resolves the ברייתא with שמואל and gives the practical rule: pause briefly after praying before urinating, without treating the place as holy.

phrases.english: Teach: "he should wait" (the time it takes to walk four cubits).
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording here, from a distance to an amount of time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: יִשְׁהֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge by correcting the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא required moving four אמות away from the place of prayer, as if that place were holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא requires only waiting the time it takes to walk four אמות. The place itself gains no holiness.

steps.title: Why wait after praying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the reason for waiting after urinating, which is the droplets. But it asks why one must wait after praying before urinating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that someone who urinated should wait the time it takes to walk four cubits, because of droplets. But someone who prayed should wait the time it takes to walk four cubits? Why do I need that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the two halves of the corrected ברייתא. It understands one half but challenges the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting after urinating before praying has a clear reason: drops of urine may still come out. Waiting after praying before urinating has no obvious reason, since the place has no lasting holiness (step 21). So the גמרא asks what this wait is for.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the part that is understood)
Droplets (of urine that may still drip out)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a return to 'moving four אמות.' After the correction in step 25, the question is only about WAITING the amount of time it takes to walk four אמות.

phrases.english: Granted, one who urinated
should wait the time it takes to walk four cubits,
because of droplets.
But one who prayed
should wait the time it takes to walk four cubits,
why do I need that?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַשְׁתִּין יִשְׁהֶה כְּדֵי הִילּוּךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, מִשּׁוּם נִיצוֹצוֹת. אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first clause of the ברייתא as it was corrected in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected first clause: one who prayed must wait four אמות' time before urinating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second clause has a clear reason (droplets), but the first clause has none, since a place of prayer has no lasting holiness.

steps.title: The prayer is still in his mouth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that for the time it takes to walk four אמות after praying, the prayer is still fresh on his lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because for the whole time of four cubits, his prayer is still arranged in his mouth, and his lips are still moving with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by giving a reason for waiting after praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not the holiness of the place. It is the person. Right after praying, his words are still on his lips. Urinating right away would show disrespect to the prayer he just said, so he waits a short moment first.

keyTerms.meaning: His prayer is (still) arranged in his mouth

steps.whatToRemember: Both waits are short and are about the person, not the place. After urinating, wait because of droplets. After praying, wait because the prayer is still on his lips.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because for the whole time of four cubits
his prayer is still arranged in his mouth,
and his lips are still moving (with it).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שֶׁכֹּל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת תְּפִלָּתוֹ סְדוּרָה בְּפִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting after prayer seemed pointless, since the place has no lasting holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wait is out of respect for the prayer, which is still fresh on the person's lips.

steps.title: Memory aid for the coming stories
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the memory aid זלפ"ן for the list of Sages who will explain why they lived long lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: ז, ל, פ, ן is the סימן (memory aid).
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to tell a series of stories, and gives letters to help remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for one Sage: ז for רבי זכאי, ל for רבי אלעזר, פ for רבי פרידא, and נ for רבי נחוניא. The link to the sugya is רבי זכאי's first merit, not urinating near a place of prayer, which connects to what we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory aid (letters to remember the order of teachings)
The letters ז-ל-פ-ן, one for each Sage

phrases.english: Zayin, Lamed, Peh, Nun is the memory aid.

steps.triggerLanguage: זַלְפָ״ן סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic discussion to a series of stories, one of which connects back to the four אמות of prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the order of the coming stories.

steps.title: Students ask רבי זכאי about his long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי's students ask him what merit earned him a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי זכאי: Through what did you live so long?
steps.whatsHappening: The first story begins. This question sets up רבי זכאי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students want to know which special good deed earned him a long life. The question opens the door to a list of practices, one of which ties back to our topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Through what (merit) did you live long?

phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Zakkai:
Through what did you live so long?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first story in the list announced by the memory aid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What merit earned רבי זכאי a long life.

steps.title: רבי זכאי's three merits
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי lists three practices: never urinating within four אמות of a place of prayer, never calling a friend by a nickname, and never missing קידוש היום. His mother once sold her head-covering to buy him wine for קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: All my days, I never urinated within four cubits of a place of prayer. I never called my friend by a nickname. And I never skipped קידוש היום. I had an old mother. Once, she sold the covering on her head and brought me wine for קידוש היום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זכאי answers his students with three special practices. He tells a story showing how careful his family was about קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first merit goes even further than the halacha we just learned. He kept away from any place of prayer, not only from where he had just prayed. The story of his mother shows how much they gave up for קידוש: she sold her own head-covering when there was no money for wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits of a place used for prayer
I gave a nickname (to embarrass someone)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Brought me קידוש היום' means she brought him wine to make קידוש on. She did not make קידוש for him.

phrases.english: He said to them:
In all my days I never urinated
within four cubits of a place of prayer,
and I never called my friend by a nickname,
and I never skipped sanctifying the day (Kiddush).
I had an old mother,
once she sold the covering on her head
and brought me (wine for) sanctifying the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִיָּמַי לֹא הִשְׁתַּנְתִּי מַיִם בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three merits: keeping away from places of prayer when urinating, never giving nicknames, and never missing קידוש, even at great cost.

steps.title: Reward of wine for honoring קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that רבי זכאי's mother left him 300 barrels of wine, and he left his sons 3,000 barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When she died, she left him three hundred barrels of wine. When he died, he left his sons three thousand barrels of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא finishes the story. It shows how רבי זכאי and his mother were rewarded for their effort to have wine for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward matches the מצוה. A family that once had no wine for קידוש ended up with huge amounts of wine. This supports the idea that great effort for קידוש brings blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זכאי lived long because of three merits. One of them, not urinating near a place of prayer, ties back to the halacha just discussed. His effort for קידוש was rewarded with great wealth in wine.

phrases.english: It was taught:
When she died, she left him
three hundred barrels of wine.
When he died, he left his sons
three thousand barrels of wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁמֵּתָה, הַנִּיחָה לוֹ שְׁלוֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that completes the story of step 30 by describing the reward.
steps.raayaObject: That the family's effort to honor קידוש was rewarded.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תנא) describing the barrels of wine they left behind.

steps.title: רב הונא pawns his belt to buy wine for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא shows up before רב wearing a straw belt. He had pawned his real belt to buy wine for קידוש. רב blesses him to be wrapped in silk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא was wearing a belt made of straw while standing before רב. רב asked him, "What is this?" He answered, "I had no wine for קידוש, so I pawned my belt and used the money to buy wine for קידוש." רב said to him, "May it be God's will that you be wrapped in silk."
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the story of רבי זכאי's mother selling her head-covering for קידוש wine, the גמרא tells a similar story about רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי זכאי's mother, רב הונא gave up a piece of his clothing so he could make קידוש on wine. His straw belt is a sign of real sacrifice. רב rewards that sacrifice with a matching blessing: instead of a cheap straw belt, he should be wrapped in silk.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece of straw or rope, used here as a cheap belt
I pawned it (gave it as security for a loan)

phrases.english: Rav Huna was girded with a straw belt
and was standing before Rav.
He (Rav) said to him: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא הֲוָה לִי קִידּוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I had no wine for Kiddush,
so I pawned my belt
and with it I brought wine for Kiddush.
phrases.notes: He used the money from pawning the belt.

phrases.english: He (Rav) said to him: May it be God's will
that you be wrapped in silk.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא הֲוָה אָסַר רִיתָא וְקָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רבי זכאי's mother: another person gives up clothing to pay for קידוש wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving up something personal in order to make קידוש on wine is a great merit, and רב blesses רב הונא for it.

steps.title: רב's blessing comes true at רבה's wedding
steps.stepSummary: At his son רבה's wedding, the short רב הונא lies on a bed without being noticed. The women of his family throw their silk garments onto him until he is covered in silk.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה, his son, got married, רב הונא was lying on a bed. He was a short man, so no one noticed him there. His daughters and daughters-in-law came in, took off their silk garments, and threw them on the bed, right on top of him. In the end he was completely wrapped in silk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב's blessing came true exactly as he said it, word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא was so short that the women did not see him lying on the bed. They piled their silk clothes on top of him, so he was literally wrapped in silk. This is the precise fulfillment of רב's words, "May you be wrapped in silk."

phrases.english: When Rabba, his son, got married,
Rav Huna, who was a short man,
was lying on a bed.
phrases.notes: Because he was short, no one noticed him.

phrases.english: His daughters and daughters-in-law came
took off their garments and threw them on him
until he was wrapped in silk.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִיכַּלַּל רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the blessing from the previous step was fulfilled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessing of a Sage was fulfilled exactly as it was spoken.

steps.title: רב is upset that רב הונא did not bless him back
steps.stepSummary: When רב hears what happened, he is upset. He asks רב הונא why he did not answer "and likewise to Master" when he was blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב heard what happened and became upset. He said, "Why didn't you say to me, when I blessed you, 'And the same for the Master'?"
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב's reaction. He wishes רב הונא had blessed him back, so he would have shared in the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב's blessing came true so exactly, it was clearly a powerful moment. If רב הונא had answered "וכן למר," the same blessing could have come true for רב as well. The lesson is that when someone blesses you, you should bless them back.

keyTerms.meaning: "and likewise to the Master" (a polite reply that returns a blessing)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's sacrifice for קידוש earned him a blessing that came true word for word. רב was upset that the blessing was not returned to him with "וכן למר."

phrases.english: Rav heard and became upset,
he said: What is the reason
that you did not say to me, when I blessed you:
"And likewise to the Master"?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע רַב וְאִיקְּפַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב reacts to the fulfillment of his blessing and closes the רב הונא story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who receives a blessing should bless the other person back with "וכן למר."

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע is asked about his long life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the זלפ"ן list. The students of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע ask him what merit earned him a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע asked him: "In what merit did you live so long?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the memory aid זלפ"ן and moves to the second Sage, the "ל" (from אלעזר). This step sets up his answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question uses the same wording that was asked of רבי זכאי. The repeated wording signals that we are moving through the list in order: ז (זכאי), then ל (אלעזר), then פ (פרידא).

keyTerms.meaning: In what merit did you live long?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse רבי אלעזר בן שמוע with רבי אלעזר (בן פדת) or רבי אליעזר. The "ל" in זלפ"ן refers to רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua:
In what merit did you live a long life?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the רב הונא side story to the זלפ"ן list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which good practices earned רבי אלעזר בן שמוע a long life.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's three practices
steps.stepSummary: He never used a בית הכנסת as a shortcut, never stepped over people sitting in the study hall, and never did ברכת כהנים without first saying the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "In all my days, I never used a בית הכנסת as a shortcut. I never stepped over the heads of the holy people. And I never raised my hands for ברכת כהנים without first saying the blessing."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע answers his students with three things he was always careful about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three practices show respect for holiness. First, a בית הכנסת is not a hallway for passing through. Second, the people learning there should not be treated with disrespect by stepping over them. Third, the כהנים' blessing must begin with its proper ברכה. This connects to the theme of the משנה, which deals with honoring a בית הכנסת.

keyTerms.meaning: a shortcut (walking through a place just to save time)
I stepped over the heads of the holy people (climbed over people seated on the floor)
I raised my hands, meaning ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: He said to them: In all my days
I never made a shortcut through a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא פָּסַעְתִּי עַל רָאשֵׁי עַם קָדוֹשׁ,
phrases.english: and I never stepped over the heads of the holy people,
phrases.notes: In the study hall, people sat on the floor. Climbing over them to reach one's seat looks disrespectful.

phrases.english: and I never raised my hands (in the Priestly Blessing) without a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִיָּמַי לֹא עָשִׂיתִי קַפֶּנְדַּרְיָא לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three practices: never using a בית הכנסת as a shortcut, never stepping over seated people, and never doing ברכת כהנים without its ברכה.

steps.title: רבי פרידא is asked about his long life
steps.stepSummary: Moving to the "פ" in זלפ"ן, the students of רבי פרידא ask him the same question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי פרידא asked him: "In what merit did you live so long?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the third Sage in the list. This step sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is word-for-word the same as before. That repeated wording is what tells us we have reached the next letter, "פ" for פרידא.

phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Perida:
In what merit did you live a long life?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי פְּרִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next name on the זלפ"ן list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which good practices earned רבי פרידא a long life.

steps.title: רבי פרידא was always first to the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא begins his answer: no one ever got to the בית המדרש before him. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "In all my days, no person ever arrived at the בית המדרש before me..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא starts listing his practices. The first is that he was always the first to arrive at the בית המדרש. His answer keeps going on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arriving first shows how much he loved learning Torah and how eager he was to be in a holy place. This is only his first practice. The rest of his answer continues in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: came before me, got there ahead of me

phrases.english: He said to them: In all my days
no person ever came before me to the study hall,
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִיָּמַי לֹא קְדָמַנִי אָדָם לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First practice: he was always the first to arrive at the בית המדרש (the answer continues on the next amud).
